claims.text: The starting alloy is eutectic Al0.7CoCrFeNi with a hierarchical dual-phase FCC+B2 lamellar microstructure.
The untreated Al0.7CoCrFeNi alloy has less than 10% room-temperature tensile elongation, approximately 8%.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal lamellar or colony boundaries cause local stress concentrations in the untreated alloy.
Boundary stress concentrations caused by dislocation pile-ups promote microcracking, brittleness, and catastrophic damage during straining.
Low-temperature annealing can precipitate nanoscale coherent L12 intermetallic particles within the FCC lamellae of Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
Annealing the as-cast alloy at approximately 500 °C for 3–5 hours is sufficient to produce the desired L12 precipitate population.
The proposed annealing treatment will produce a uniform L12 dispersion, particularly along or near internal lamellar boundaries.
Coherent L12 nanoparticles impede dislocation motion through Orowan bowing or bypass.
The L12 nanoparticles promote alternative dislocation paths and a more gradual distribution of dislocations.
The L12 nanoparticle dispersion reduces dislocation pile-ups at internal lamellar boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups will lower local stress concentrations and suppress microcrack nucleation.
The annealed alloy will deform more homogeneously than the untreated alloy.
Low-temperature L12 precipitation can increase the strength of Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
The treatment will increase room-temperature tensile elongation from approximately 8% to greater than 20%.
The treated alloy will maintain or increase yield strength to approximately 1070 MPa or higher.
A quasi-static tensile strain rate of approximately 10^-3 s^-1 is applicable for evaluating the proposed treatment.
Over-aging, nonuniform precipitation, excessive recrystallization, or precipitate coarsening could prevent the intended ductility improvement.
The intervention should apply to other eutectic high-entropy alloys having dual-phase lamellar structures similar to Al0.7CoCrFeNi.
